name: Swiss-German Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Forschungszentrum für Gebärdensprache Basel, publication lists (deutsch/) and VUGS Informationsheft series index (issues 1-48 downloadable)
sources.note: Bibliographic pages only; scanned for prosody/phonology titles. Only VUGS 27 (age of acquisition, incl. prosody) and VUGS 35 (Steiner 2000, eyebrow raise, nonmanual) touch suprasegmentals; no DSGS item on stress/Betonung listed.

sources.citation: Boyes Braem, Penny. 2024. Gebärdensprachen. In Glaser, Kabatek & Sonnenhauser (eds.), Sprachenräume der Schweiz. Band 1: Sprachen, 185-209. Tübingen: Narr.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Most recent overview of DSGS by the principal researcher; CC BY-SA open access but the Narr eLibrary viewer is JS-only (PDF not retrievable by automated download); low chance of a stress statement but would confirm the state of description.

sources.citation: Boyes Braem, Penny. 1995. Eine Untersuchung über den Einfluss des Erwerbsalters auf die in der deutschsprachigen Schweiz verwendeten Formen von Gebärdensprache. VUGS Informationsheft Nr. 27. Zürich: Verein zur Unterstützung der Gebärdensprache der Gehörlosen. 70 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on lexical/sign-internal stress. Prosody treated only at utterance level: sec. 4.1 'Zeitfaktoren in der Erzeugung von Äusserungen' (p.27) describes 'zeitliches Ausgleichen' (temporal balancing) of phrases marking utterance boundaries; sec. 4.2.D (p.36) 'Oberkörperbewegung als eine rhythmische prosodische Struktureinheit' describes rhythmic torso sway over several signs returning to neutral at the end of sentences/sentence groups (scanned of PDF pp. 35, 42-46).

sources.citation: Boyes-Braem, Penny. 1995. Einführung in die Gebärdensprache und ihre Erforschung. 3rd rev. ed. Hamburg: Signum. 240 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's main descriptive reference for DSGS; German-language introduction to sign structure with DSGS data; the likeliest place for any remark on Betonung/stress as a movement modification in DSGS signs.

sources.citation: Ebling, S., Tissi, K., Sidler-Miserez, S., Schlupf, C. & Boyes Braem, P. 2021. Single-parameter and parameter combination errors in L2 productions of Swiss German Sign Language. Sign Language & Linguistics 24(2): 143-181.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Modern treatment of DSGS phonological parameters (handshape, location, movement, nonmanuals); could mention movement/prominence features, though focused on L2 errors.

sources.citation: Boyes Braem, Penny. 1999. Rhythmic temporal patterns in the signing of deaf early and late learners of Swiss German Sign Language. Language and Speech 42(2-3): 177-208.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only dedicated study of DSGS prosody (in the Sandler-edited L&S prosody issue alongside Wilbur's ASL stress paper); full text may discuss sign-level prominence/holds and would be the primary citation for any DSGS prosodic statement.

sources.note: Glottolog 'overview' entry; print only, not opened. General introduction to sign language structure with DSGS examples; may discuss Betonung as movement modification but unverified.
